title: Short-Term Rental DSCR Loans by Colorado Mountain Town: Licensing Rules in Summit, Eagle, Routt and Pitkin County
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

If you are considering a short-term rental in Colorado’s mountain communities, local operating rules belong near the beginning of your financing research. The property’s jurisdiction, zone and license status can affect whether the intended use is allowed. A lender separately determines whether and how rental income can be used for qualification.

Confirm the jurisdiction first

A county name does not identify the complete rule set for every property within it. Incorporated municipalities and unincorporated areas may follow different licensing and zoning systems. Start with the exact property address and the government responsible for its intended rental use.

Ask whether a license is required, whether the property’s zone permits the use, whether a cap or pause applies, and whether an existing license can transfer to a buyer. Verify any property-specific restrictions instead of relying on an old listing or a general county summary.

Short-term rental rules by Colorado county and town

Sources reviewed September 21, 2026. This table summarizes published rules and directs you to the responsible office; it does not certify that an individual property can operate. Availability, pauses, permit conditions and transfer rules can change. Obtain an address-specific answer before relying on rental income, and recheck before closing.

How local rules connect with DSCR financing

A rental-income estimate should be supported by an operating plan that can be carried out lawfully. If short-term rental operation is restricted, the lender may evaluate a different income basis or may not accept the proposed scenario. Confirm the available treatment with the lender; do not assume that long-term rent will automatically provide an acceptable fallback.

Even when a short-term rental is permitted, the lender may impose its own requirements for income history, appraisal, occupancy assumptions, property type and documentation. Local approval is not loan approval.

Questions to resolve before relying on a property’s income

• Which jurisdiction and zone govern this address?

• What license or registration is needed, and can a new owner obtain it?

• Are caps, waitlists, moratoriums or transfer restrictions relevant?

• Are there association, deed or property-specific restrictions to investigate?

• What rental-income evidence will the lender accept?

• How does the financing scenario change if the intended short-term use is unavailable?

Who to contact

Use the relevant official municipal or county office for operating-rule questions and the lender for financing requirements. Save the source link, contact details and date checked for each jurisdiction. For property-specific uncertainty, obtain the appropriate professional or official clarification.

Frequently asked questions

Does an existing vacation-rental listing prove that I can operate after buying?

No. Confirm the current rules, license status and any transfer restrictions for the property and new owner.

Are county and town rules interchangeable?

No. Determine whether the property is inside a municipality or in an unincorporated area and check the correct authority.

Will a lender accept projected short-term rental income?

Only if the selected program and documentation requirements allow the scenario. Ask Jerry which documentation the selected lender accepts.

title: DSCR Loan Requirements in Colorado: Minimum Ratio, Credit Score and Down Payment
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

DSCR loan requirements vary by lender and property. A Colorado investor should confirm the qualifying rental-income calculation, credit, down payment, reserves and property rules for the specific program being considered. There is no single statewide DSCR program or universal minimum credit score. Compare written requirements for the actual loan under consideration.

Start with the lender’s calculation

Ask which rental-income evidence the lender accepts and which payment components it includes. A lease, appraisal-based market rent or permitted short-term rental income may be treated differently. The resulting ratio is a lender qualification measure, not a complete investment-profitability analysis.

Requirements by ratio profile

Other details to confirm

• Credit requirements and how borrower history is reviewed.

• Minimum down payment, maximum loan-to-value and reserve requirements.

• Eligible property types, unit counts and condition requirements.

• Whether an LLC or other ownership structure is accepted.

• Rental-income documentation and short-term rental treatment.

• Closing costs, pricing, prepayment terms and any other restrictions.

How to improve your position

A better-supported rent figure, more equity, stronger credit and documented reserves can improve the options available. Obtain realistic insurance and tax estimates early. Lowering an estimated payment on paper does not help if the final costs are higher. Ask Jerry to compare the same property under the available programs.

What changes for Colorado investors?

The local layer is often the property’s permitted rental use. A town’s zoning or licensing rules can affect whether a planned short-term rental operation is allowed. That does not replace lender underwriting: a property must meet both the relevant local requirements and the financing program’s rules.

Preparing a useful loan discussion

Bring the property address, intended rental use, available lease or rent information, ownership plan and the funds available for the transaction. Ask Jerry which assumptions are still estimates and which can be supported by current documents. A clear scenario makes it easier to compare actual options.

Frequently asked questions

Is there one minimum DSCR for all Colorado loans?

No. Requirements vary by lender and product. The ratio examples explain the math; they do not establish eligibility for a particular loan.

Does a larger down payment guarantee a better offer?

It may affect the available terms, but the full borrower and property review still matters. Obtain a scenario-specific comparison.

Can I qualify using projected Airbnb income?

The answer depends on local operating rules and the lender’s accepted income documentation and calculation.

title: DSCR Loans in Colorado: The Complete 2026 Guide for Real Estate Investors
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

A DSCR loan may help a real estate investor qualify using a property’s rental income rather than personal tax returns as the main income measure. For Colorado investors, it is important to understand both the lender’s requirements and the local rules affecting the property’s intended rental use.

In this guide

DSCR loan requirements

DSCR loans and mountain-town short-term rentals

Colorado DSCR loan FAQs

What DSCR means

DSCR stands for debt service coverage ratio. For many residential investment-loan programs, a lender compares qualifying rental income with the applicable housing payment. The exact income figure, payment components and documentation are determined by the lender’s program.

Meeting a ratio alone does not guarantee loan approval. Credit, down payment, reserves, property eligibility, ownership structure and other underwriting requirements may also apply.

How a lender may calculate the ratio

A common calculation divides qualifying monthly rent by principal, interest, taxes, insurance and association dues, often shortened to PITIA. The selected lender decides how to document rent and which costs to include.

A ratio of 1.0 under a particular calculation means the counted income equals the counted payment. It does not establish that the property breaks even after all operating expenses, vacancy, maintenance and other costs. Evaluate investment cash flow separately.

The figures above are an arithmetic example, not a rate quote, actual transaction or promise of approval. They exclude vacancy, management, repairs and other operating expenses.

How DSCR financing compares with conventional financing

DSCR products may be useful when a borrower’s personal tax returns do not represent the basis the lender will use for rental-property qualification. Compare the available options using the same property and borrower scenario. Review rate, down payment, reserves, closing costs, prepayment terms and documentation requirements together.

Property types and ownership

Long-term rentals, short-term rentals and two-to-four-unit investment properties may be eligible. Whether a specific property or ownership structure qualifies depends on the chosen product. Ask about property condition, appraisal and rent documentation early in the process.

Short-term rentals in Colorado

Mountain communities can have different licensing, zoning, cap and operating requirements. Rules for an incorporated town may differ from those for surrounding unincorporated county areas. Confirm the jurisdiction and the property’s intended use before relying on projected short-term rental income.

A lender may apply different rules to short-term rental income than to a long-term lease or market-rent appraisal. Local permission to operate and lender acceptance of the income are separate questions.

See the dated Colorado mountain-town STR guide for official sources and the broader county-by-county comparison.

Rates, costs and transaction review

DSCR pricing and terms vary by lender, borrower and property. Ratio, loan-to-value, credit, property type and other factors may influence the available offer. Obtain a scenario-specific review rather than treating a general article as a current rate quote.

DSCR financing is one of Jerry’s focus areas at Independent Mortgage Brokers. His approach starts with the property and your plans, then works through the numbers and available options in plain language.

A practical starting sequence

• Identify the property, ownership plan and intended rental use.

• Check the correct local jurisdiction and any rental restrictions.

• Ask how the lender will document and calculate rental income.

• Review the full requirements, estimated costs and available terms.

• Complete application, appraisal and underwriting, then review final closing figures.

Frequently asked questions

Can a DSCR loan be used for a Colorado short-term rental?

It may be possible under an eligible lender program and local rules. Both the property’s permitted use and the lender’s income treatment need review.

Does a strong ratio mean I am automatically approved?

No. The ratio is only part of the lender’s underwriting review.

Can I buy through an LLC?

Some products may allow an entity borrower, but the ownership and documentation requirements must be confirmed with Jerry’s lenders.

Michael Angelini’s review highlights Jerry’s responsiveness and willingness to answer questions. These are general mortgage-service reviews, not claims about a particular VA or DSCR transaction. title: Frequently Asked Questions: VA Loans in Colorado
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

These answers cover common VA loan questions for Colorado veterans and military families. Eligibility, entitlement and the details of a particular transaction matter, so use these answers as a starting point for a lender conversation.

Eligibility and entitlement

Who qualifies for a VA loan in Colorado?

Eligible veterans, active-duty service members, some National Guard and Reserve members, and certain surviving spouses may qualify. VA service requirements and a Certificate of Eligibility are part of the review.

Can National Guard or Reserve members qualify?

They may qualify depending on the length and type of service and the applicable VA rules. The required documents vary by service history. VA reviews qualifying active service or other eligible Guard/Reserve service paths.

Can I use a VA loan more than once?

Potentially. Ask a lender to review prior use, remaining entitlement and any restoration requirements.

Does my COE mean the loan is approved?

No. It documents VA eligibility information. The lender must still review the borrower, property and other loan requirements.

Down payment, fees and costs

Do I need a down payment?

Many eligible VA purchases do not require a down payment. Available entitlement, lender approval, the appraisal and transaction details can affect the result.

Do VA loans have PMI?

VA-backed loans do not charge monthly private mortgage insurance. A funding fee may apply unless an exemption is available.

What is the VA funding fee?

It is a one-time program fee. The applicable amount depends on the loan type and other relevant factors, including first/subsequent use and down payment where applicable.

Are all veterans exempt from the funding fee?

No. Exemption depends on VA’s qualifying categories and documentation. Confirm the status for your transaction rather than assuming it applies.

Does no down payment mean no closing costs?

No. Closing costs and other cash requirements should be reviewed separately. Ask for the full loan estimate and any applicable seller credits or financing options.

Documentation and the buying process

Do I need my COE before speaking with a lender?

No. You can begin the discussion while the certificate is being obtained. Your lender can explain which documents are needed next.

How long does a VA purchase take in Colorado?

Timing depends on documentation, appraisal, property conditions and underwriting. Discuss your target date with Jerry early so the loan steps can be coordinated with your contract and move.

What does the VA appraisal review?

It supports the value and property-requirement review for the loan. It is not a substitute for a separate home inspection.

Can I begin planning before PCS orders are final?

You can discuss your expected move and financing needs. The lender should confirm which documents and occupancy or employment details will be needed as the transaction progresses.

After closing and related benefits

Can I refinance a VA loan later?

A refinance may be available if the applicable requirements are met. The IRRRL is designed for eligible existing VA loans; other refinance options have different requirements.

Does a VA loan automatically qualify me for Colorado’s disabled-veteran property tax exemption?

No. The state tax benefit has separate eligibility, property and application rules. Check the current official Colorado instructions.

title: VA Certificate of Eligibility: Step-by-Step for Colorado Veterans and Reservists
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

Your Certificate of Eligibility, or COE, helps a lender confirm eligibility for a VA home loan. It can also provide entitlement and funding-fee exemption information. Colorado veterans, active-duty service members, Guard and Reserve members, and eligible surviving spouses may have different document requirements.

What the COE confirms

The COE documents VA eligibility information. It does not guarantee that a lender will approve a particular loan or property. Credit, income, entitlement, appraisal and other applicable requirements still need to be reviewed.

You can begin talking with a lender before you have the certificate in hand. The lender can help identify the request route and any missing service documentation.

Three ways to request a COE

1. Through your loan officer

A lender may be able to obtain the COE electronically. Some records can be confirmed quickly; other cases require additional information or VA review. Ask what documents the lender needs and when to expect an update.

2. Through VA online

You can use VA’s official online request process. Follow the current instructions for signing in, selecting your eligibility category and supplying documents.

3. By mail when appropriate

Use VA Form 26-1880 for the standard mailed COE request. VA notes that mailed requests may take longer than online or lender requests. Surviving spouses should follow the separate instructions for their situation.

Documents to prepare

Start with VA’s official COE request page for the online request, current forms and full document checklist. Share service records through the secure channel your lender or VA provides.

Common reasons for delays

Documents that are incomplete, do not show the required service information, or do not match the request category can lead to follow-up questions. A previous use of the VA benefit may also require a closer entitlement review. Ask your loan officer what is missing rather than repeatedly submitting the same material without clarification.

After the COE is available

Review the certificate with your lender, including entitlement and any exemption information relevant to the loan. Then confirm the remaining pre-approval or underwriting steps. Keep your planned purchase or relocation timeline in the conversation.

Frequently asked questions

Do I need the COE before my first lender conversation?

No. You can start the conversation and ask for help with the request.

Can Jerry obtain it in the first call?

Some COEs are available electronically; others require additional records or VA review. Jerry can help you identify the right request path and what is needed next.

Does a COE mean I am fully approved?

No. It confirms VA eligibility information; the lender must complete the other applicable reviews.

title: Property Tax Exemption for Disabled Veterans in Colorado: How It Works With a VA Loan
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

Colorado offers a property tax exemption for certain qualifying disabled veterans and surviving spouses. For a homeowner with a VA loan, the benefit may reduce property taxes and potentially affect the tax portion of mortgage escrow. Qualification for a VA mortgage does not automatically establish eligibility for this state tax benefit.

What the exemption does

The exemption removes a qualifying portion of a residence’s value from the property tax calculation. That is different from receiving the same dollar amount as a tax refund or a direct reduction in the mortgage balance. Actual savings depend on the applicable tax calculation and the property.

For a qualifying primary residence, the exemption covers 50% of the first $200,000 of actual property value. That means up to $100,000 of value is excluded—not a $100,000 tax credit. For example, a qualifying home valued at $175,000 has $87,500 of exempt value. Your assessor calculates the actual tax effect.

Confirm your eligibility before applying

Gather the documents required by the current application instructions and review the specific eligibility category that applies to you. State property tax rules and VA funding-fee exemptions are separate; qualifying for one does not by itself prove eligibility for the other.

The state’s criteria include qualifying active-duty service and an honorable discharge, plus a VA-established 100% permanent service-connected disability or individual unemployability status. The applicant or spouse must generally own the home, and the applicant must occupy it as a primary residence, on January 1 of the application year. Separate applications cover a surviving spouse of a veteran who previously received the exemption and qualifying Gold Star spouses. Check the state instructions for your category and any exceptions.

How to apply

• Use the Colorado Division of Property Taxation application and instructions for your eligibility category.

• File with the county assessor where the property is located. Prepare the current VA award letter and the supporting service, ownership or spouse documents required by your form.

• Submit through the approved channel and keep confirmation of receipt.

• Follow up with the appropriate office about approval and how the exemption appears on the property’s tax record.

Application deadline update: Colorado SB26-046, effective August 12, 2026, aligns the regular application deadline at July 15 and the late deadline at August 15. Some older state and county instructions still show July 1/August 1. As of September 21, 2026, these annual windows have passed. Ask your assessor about the next application year, current forms and appeal rights before filing.

How tax savings may affect a VA loan payment

When property taxes are paid through a mortgage escrow account, a lower tax obligation may change the required escrow payment. The loan servicer’s analysis and timing determine when that change is reflected. An exemption does not change the loan’s principal-and-interest terms, and it should not be described as an immediate guaranteed payment reduction.

Frequently asked questions

Can this be used alongside a VA funding-fee exemption?

They are separate benefits. Some homeowners may qualify for both, but each has its own eligibility requirements.

Does refinancing automatically end the exemption?

Review the current state and county rules for the property, ownership and occupancy. Confirm any reporting obligations before assuming the exemption continues unchanged.

Will my monthly payment drop as soon as I apply?

An application is not an approval. Any escrow change also depends on the approved tax treatment and the servicer’s processing and analysis.

title: VA Funding Fees in Colorado: 2026 Rates and Examples
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

The VA funding fee is a one-time cost associated with many VA home loans. It helps support the program and is separate from interest and other closing costs. Some borrowers are exempt. For Colorado buyers, understanding the applicable fee and whether it will be paid at closing or financed can help clarify the loan estimate.

What determines the funding fee?

The fee depends on the type of VA loan and the applicable program rules. For purchase loans, first or subsequent use and down payment can affect the percentage. Refinances and other loan types have their own rules. Exemption status must also be considered.

The fee is based on the applicable loan amount, rather than simply using the home’s purchase price. A down payment can change both the loan amount and the relevant purchase fee bracket.

2026 funding-fee reference table

Official reference: VA funding fee and loan closing costs.

Who may be exempt?

VA lists exemptions for borrowers receiving service-connected disability compensation; those entitled to it but receiving retirement or active-duty pay instead; qualifying surviving spouses receiving Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC); certain service members with a proposed or memorandum rating before closing; and active-duty Purple Heart recipients who provide evidence by closing. Your lender confirms the applicable status and documentation.

How to calculate your funding fee

Calculation concept: applicable loan amount × verified funding-fee percentage = estimated funding fee.

For an illustrative $400,000 base purchase loan, a non-exempt first-time user in the less-than-5%-down bracket has a $8,600 funding fee: $400,000 × 0.0215. Financing only that fee produces a $408,600 loan balance. A borrower who is exempt would have no funding fee. This example uses a round loan amount, not a claimed Colorado median, and excludes other costs.

If you finance the fee, you also pay interest on that additional balance. A later VA compensation award may support a fee refund when its effective date is before the loan closing; ask your lender or VA to review your case. Colorado’s veteran property-tax exemption has separate eligibility rules.

Frequently asked questions

Can the funding fee be financed?

It can generally be included in an eligible VA loan, but confirm the rules for your loan type and how it changes the balance. Other closing costs may be treated differently.

How do I know whether I am exempt?

Ask your lender to confirm your eligibility and the documentation needed for the exemption.

Is the funding fee the same as a down payment?

No. They are different costs with different purposes. A transaction may have no down payment and still include a funding fee or other closing costs.

Does first use always mean the same rate?

No. The applicable loan type, down payment where relevant and exemption status must be evaluated.

content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

Colorado Springs and El Paso County are home to military families connected with Fort Carson, Peterson Space Force Base, Schriever Space Force Base and the U.S. Air Force Academy. If you are buying with a VA loan while planning a military move, preparing your eligibility documents and understanding the local purchase process can help you make informed decisions.

Start with your timeline and financing

A PCS move can create several overlapping deadlines: reporting dates, housing arrangements, a home search and loan closing. Begin by discussing your plans with a loan officer, including when orders are expected, when you need to move and whether you are selling another property. Avoid assuming that every step can be completed on a fixed schedule.

Obtaining a COE and discussing pre-approval early can identify questions about eligibility, entitlement and required documents before you make an offer. Occupancy and relocation circumstances should be reviewed for your specific situation.

Plan your home search around your installation

The right location depends on more than a base name. Work location, commute preferences, budget, property type and your household’s needs all matter. Use current local information and your own priorities when comparing neighborhoods.

A practical PCS purchase sequence

• Discuss eligibility, entitlement, budget and the expected move with the lender.

• Collect service, employment and other requested documents.

• Coordinate the home search and offer timeline with your real estate professional.

• Allow time for appraisal, any property conditions and underwriting.

• Confirm final closing arrangements before making firm moving commitments.

Property questions that deserve an early review

Ask about property condition, access, utilities and any well or septic systems before you rely on a particular financing plan. The VA appraisal and lender review may identify conditions to resolve. A separate home inspection helps you understand the property and is not replaced by the appraisal.

For installation housing and relocation contacts, use Military OneSource’s official installation directory. Check travel routes yourself and choose a location based on your household’s priorities.

Working with a local loan officer

Ask how your loan officer handles military timelines, communicates about documents and coordinates with the people involved in your purchase. Jerry is a lifelong Coloradan, and his approach centers on explaining options and keeping the next steps clear. Bring your expected reporting date and housing plans to the first conversation.

Frequently asked questions

Can I start before my orders are final?

You can begin a planning conversation and ask which documents are available now and which must follow. Your lender should review the effect of your expected move on qualification and occupancy.

Will I need a down payment?

Many eligible VA purchases require no down payment, but entitlement, lender approval, appraisal and transaction details affect the answer. Closing costs may still apply.

How long should I allow for closing?

Ask for a current estimate based on your transaction. Appraisal, property issues, documentation and underwriting can all affect timing.

title: VA Home Loans in Colorado: The Complete 2026 Guide for Veterans and Active-Duty Buyers
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

If you have served in the military, a VA home loan may be an important option when buying or refinancing a home. In Colorado, local factors such as military relocation timelines, property conditions and state benefits can shape the questions you need to ask. This guide introduces the VA loan process and practical resources for Colorado veterans and active-duty buyers.

In this guide

VA loans and PCS moves in Colorado Springs

VA funding fees and examples

Colorado veteran property-tax exemption

How to request your VA Certificate of Eligibility

Colorado VA loan FAQs

What a VA loan is and how it works in Colorado

A VA-backed home loan is a mortgage made by a private lender with a guaranty from the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs. That guaranty can support benefits such as no required down payment in many eligible purchase scenarios and no monthly mortgage insurance. The lender still reviews your ability to qualify and the property being financed.

VA-backed loans are different from the Native American Direct Loan program, in which VA is the lender for eligible borrowers and properties. Availability and requirements depend on the program.

Eligibility and the Certificate of Eligibility

Eligibility depends on service history and duty status. Active-duty service members generally meet the minimum service requirement after 90 continuous days; requirements for Veterans depend on when and how they served. Separate qualifying paths apply to National Guard and Reserve members, and certain surviving spouses may qualify. A Certificate of Eligibility, or COE, documents the borrower’s service-based eligibility and entitlement information.

The COE is one part of the process. It does not replace the lender’s credit, income, property and underwriting review.

Down payment and mortgage insurance

Many eligible VA purchases can be completed without a down payment, but the amount you can borrow and any cash needed depend on available entitlement, lender approval, the property’s appraised value and the transaction. No down payment does not mean there are no closing costs.

VA-backed loans do not charge monthly private mortgage insurance. A VA funding fee may apply unless the borrower qualifies for an exemption. Compare the full loan costs rather than focusing only on a single benefit.

The VA funding fee

The VA funding fee is a one-time program cost that may be financed or paid at closing. For a purchase loan with less than 5% down, the current fee is 2.15% for first use and 3.3% after first use. It falls to 1.5% with at least 5% down and 1.25% with at least 10% down. Certain borrowers are exempt, including qualifying recipients of service-connected disability compensation, qualifying surviving spouses receiving DIC and qualifying active-duty Purple Heart recipients.

Entitlement and county loan limits

Entitlement is the amount VA may guarantee to the lender. The $36,000 basic-entitlement figure shown on many COEs is not the borrower’s maximum loan amount. Borrowers with full entitlement do not have a VA-imposed loan limit, although lender qualification, purchase price and appraisal value still limit the transaction. When a borrower has reduced entitlement, remaining entitlement is calculated using the applicable county conforming loan limit and entitlement already charged.

VA, FHA and conventional financing

Compare loan options using the same property, budget and expected time in the home. Ask for a side-by-side review of cash needed at closing, monthly payment, mortgage insurance and total borrowing costs. The summary below describes program differences; it is not an offer of specific loan terms.

Purchase, refinance and related VA benefits

VA home loan options include purchase loans, the Interest Rate Reduction Refinance Loan (IRRRL) for eligible existing VA loans, and cash-out refinancing. The Native American Direct Loan has separate eligibility and property requirements. Adapted-housing grants are grants, rather than an additional mortgage type. Energy-efficiency improvements may also be addressed through applicable program options.

The steps and timing from preparation to closing

There is no single guaranteed VA closing timeframe. Contract deadlines, borrower documentation, appraisal availability, property conditions and underwriting all affect the schedule. Jerry can provide a realistic target after reviewing the transaction.

• Discuss budget, documents and pre-approval with your lender.

• Choose a home and review any Colorado property-specific considerations.

• Complete the appraisal and required inspections; an appraisal is not a substitute for a home inspection.

• Resolve underwriting conditions, review closing figures and complete closing.

Colorado considerations

Military families around Colorado Springs may be coordinating a purchase with PCS orders. Rural and mountain properties can raise questions about access, utilities, wells, septic systems and condition. Some qualifying disabled veterans may also be eligible for a Colorado property tax benefit, subject to separate state requirements.

Jerry is a lifelong Coloradan who grew up in Commerce City and lives in Aurora. His work with Independent Mortgage Brokers includes VA financing and refinancing. The goal is a clear comparison of your options and a next step you understand.

Questions to discuss with Jerry

Can I use my VA benefit again?

Possibly. Ask for an entitlement review, including any prior VA loan use and restoration requirements.

Can I start before I have my COE?

You can begin a discussion with a lender while the COE is being obtained. The lender will explain what is needed for the next stage.

Which local guide should I read next?

Our Colorado resources cover Colorado Springs, the funding fee, Colorado’s disabled-veteran property tax exemption, the COE and VA FAQs.

What clients value about working with Jerry

Paul Giron’s public review describes dependable help across multiple mortgages and prompt communication. Michael Angelini’s review highlights Jerry’s responsiveness and willingness to answer questions. These are general mortgage-service reviews, not claims about a particular VA or DSCR transaction. title: Frequently Asked Questions: DSCR Loans in Colorado
content:
Last reviewed: September 21, 2026

These answers address common questions about DSCR financing for Colorado investment properties. Program rules differ by lender, and short-term rental use adds local questions that must be checked for the specific property.

Qualifying and documenting income

What does DSCR stand for?

Debt service coverage ratio. It compares a lender-defined measure of rental income with the applicable debt or housing payment. Confirm the exact program calculation.

Do DSCR loans use personal tax returns to qualify?

These programs generally focus on property rental income for income qualification. The lender still determines the documents and other borrower information required. Ask Jerry which program fits your property.

What minimum ratio do I need?

There is no single minimum across all lenders. A ratio of 1.0 means qualifying rent equals the counted payment; 1.25 means rent is 25% higher. Ask for the actual program minimum and how the lender documents rent.

Does meeting the ratio guarantee approval?

No. Credit, down payment, reserves, property eligibility and other underwriting requirements can still apply.

Does a ratio of 1.0 mean the property is profitable?

No. It means the counted income equals the counted payment under that calculation. Operating expenses, vacancy and other costs require a separate cash-flow review.

Properties, ownership and short-term rentals

Can I use a DSCR loan for an Airbnb in Colorado?

It may be possible if the lender accepts the property and income scenario and the intended use complies with local rules.

Do two-to-four-unit properties qualify?

Some programs may accept them. Confirm the selected lender’s unit-count, property and rental-income requirements.

Can the borrower be an LLC?

Some products may allow an entity borrower. Ownership, guarantees and documentation must be reviewed under the program’s rules.

Does an existing STR license automatically transfer to me?

Do not assume it does. Transfer and new-owner rules must be verified with the correct local jurisdiction.

Can I use long-term rent if short-term rental use is restricted?

Ask the lender whether an acceptable long-term rental scenario is available and how it would change qualification. It is not an automatic substitute.

Costs and terms

How much down payment will I need?

The required amount depends on the program, borrower and property. Ask for the maximum loan-to-value and the cash needed for down payment, closing costs and reserves as separate figures.

How are DSCR loan rates determined?

Rates and pricing can vary with the lender, market and transaction details. Ask for a current scenario-specific quote and compare total costs and terms.

Will I need reserves?

Reserve requirements depend on the product and scenario. Confirm how much is required and which assets are eligible.

Process and preparation

How long does a DSCR loan take to close?

Timing depends on documents, appraisal, property issues and underwriting. Ask Jerry for a target based on your property, document readiness and contract deadlines.

What should I prepare for the first conversation?

Bring the property address, intended rental use, available lease or rent information, ownership plan and an outline of the funds available for the transaction. Ask which assumptions need documentation.

title: Good Neighbor Next Door Program in Colorado: Eligibility, HUD Homes & How It Works
content:
Buying a home can feel overwhelming. If you are a Colorado teacher, law enforcement officer, firefighter, or emergency medical technician, the Good Neighbor Next Door program may make the process more affordable. An eligible buyer may be able to purchase a select HUD home for 50% off the list price. With qualifying FHA financing, the down payment may be as little as $100.

Those benefits sound exciting, but the program has important rules. The buyer, job, home, location, and loan all need to qualify. Eligible homes are also hard to find. This guide breaks everything into simple steps so you can understand the program without feeling like you need to become a mortgage expert.

What Is the Good Neighbor Next Door Program?

The Good Neighbor Next Door Sales Program, also called GNND, is offered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, or HUD. It helps certain community professionals buy a HUD-owned home in an area HUD is working to improve.

The program does not work with every home for sale. You cannot choose any Colorado house and ask HUD to take 50% off the price. The home must be owned by HUD, approved for the program, and located in a HUD-designated revitalization area. In plain English, that means HUD has chosen the home and neighborhood for this special program.

Good Neighbor Next Door Benefits at a Glance

  • 50% off the list price of an eligible Good Neighbor Next Door home
  • Possibly as little as $100 down with qualifying FHA financing
  • A choice of FHA, VA, conventional financing, or cash
  • A possible FHA 203(k) renovation loan if the home needs repairs
  • A chance to buy a select HUD home before it is offered to other buyers

You still need to qualify for your mortgage. A lender will review your income, credit, debts, savings, and the home itself. You may also need money for closing costs, inspections, insurance, and repairs. Jerry can help you understand what may apply before you make an offer.

How the 50% Good Neighbor Next Door Discount Works

You make an offer at HUD’s full list price, but you pay or finance only half of that amount at closing. HUD keeps track of the other half with a second mortgage. This second mortgage protects the discount while you complete the program’s three-year living requirement.

Here is a simple example. If an eligible HUD home is listed for $300,000, the discounted price would be $150,000. HUD would record a second mortgage for the other $150,000. This is only an example. The price, loan, costs, and homes available in Colorado will be different for every buyer.

What Is the Silent Second Mortgage?

The HUD second mortgage is often called a silent second mortgage. “Silent” means you do not make a monthly payment on it, and it does not charge interest while you follow the program rules.

You must live in the home for three years and complete the forms HUD sends you each year. After you finish those requirements, HUD can release the second mortgage. If you move, sell, or stop using the home as your main home too early, you may have to repay part or all of the discount. Talk with HUD and your loan professional before selling or refinancing during those three years.

How the $100 Down Payment Option Works

If you qualify for Good Neighbor Next Door and use qualifying FHA-insured financing, your down payment may be only $100. In some cases, certain closing costs may be included in the FHA loan. The home, loan amount, appraisal, and current program rules all matter.

Keep in mind that “$100 down” does not mean “only $100 needed.” You may still pay for an inspection, earnest money, taxes, homeowners insurance, mortgage insurance, repairs, and other closing costs. Once you choose a home and loan, your lender will give you a clearer estimate of how much money you may need.

Could $100 Down Apply Without the GNND Discount?

It may. HUD also has an FHA $100 Down Sales Incentive for certain HUD-owned homes. A buyer who does not qualify for the Good Neighbor Next Door discount may still find an eligible HUD home that allows qualifying FHA financing with as little as $100 down.

Not every HUD home offers this option. The property listing, the FHA loan, and the lender must all allow it. Jerry can help check whether a Colorado home is eligible and whether FHA financing through UWM or another available lending option may fit your needs. Approval is never automatic.

Who Qualifies for the Neighbor Next Door Program?

The GNND program is for four groups of full-time community professionals. Your job title is only the starting point. HUD will also look at who employs you and whether you serve the area where the home is located.

Law Enforcement Officers and Police Officers

You may qualify if you work full time for a federal, state, local, or tribal law enforcement agency. You must be sworn to uphold the law and make arrests. Your normal work must directly serve the area where the home is located.

Pre-K Through 12 Teachers

You may qualify if you are a full-time teacher at a state-accredited public or private school serving students from pre-kindergarten through grade 12. The students you normally serve must come from the area where the home is located.

Firefighters and Emergency Medical Technicians

You may qualify if you work full time as a firefighter or emergency medical technician for a federal, state, local, or tribal fire department or emergency services unit. Your normal work must serve the area where the home is located.

Other first responders, military members, school employees, healthcare workers, volunteers, and public servants do not qualify based on those jobs alone. They would need to meet HUD’s definition for one of the four approved professions.

Other GNND Buyer Eligibility Rules

You do not have to be a first-time homebuyer. However, HUD’s current GNND consumer fact sheet says that you and your spouse generally cannot own another home when you submit your offer or during the 12 months before your offer.

You must plan in good faith to stay in your eligible full-time job for at least one year after closing. You must also qualify for your chosen loan. GNND does not have one simple household income limit, but your income, credit, savings, debts, and job history will affect the mortgage options available to you.

What Homes Are Eligible in Colorado?

The 50% discount applies only to select HUD-owned single-family homes in approved areas. An eligible property might be a detached house, townhouse, or condo. HUD sells these homes “as is,” which means HUD will not fix the home or provide a home warranty.

GNND homes are usually listed for the program for seven days. If more than one qualified buyer wants the same home, HUD chooses the buyer through a random lottery. Available properties are limited, and the list can change every week. This is why you may see no Colorado homes one week and a new listing later.

Why Limited Inventory Matters

You cannot control when an eligible home becomes available. It helps to review your job and loan eligibility first, so you are better prepared when the right home appears. You may need to act quickly, but you should never feel rushed into skipping an inspection or ignoring repair costs.

It is okay if there is no home available today. Checking the listings regularly and having a plan can make the process feel much more manageable.

How to Buy a Good Neighbor Next Door Home

  1. Check your job eligibility. Make sure your profession, employer, and service area meet HUD’s rules.
  2. Talk about financing. Review FHA, VA, conventional, and cash options. Ask about the $100-down option before you bid.
  3. Watch for Colorado HUD homes. Check the HUD Home Store regularly because listings may change weekly.
  4. Choose a HUD-registered real estate broker. The broker helps you find the home and send your offer to HUD.
  5. Offer the full list price. HUD does not negotiate the GNND list price. The program applies the 50% discount separately.
  6. Wait for the result. If several qualified buyers want the same home, HUD uses a lottery.
  7. Review the home and loan carefully. Look at the inspection, appraisal, repairs, insurance, monthly payment, and closing costs.
  8. Close and move in. You will sign your loan papers and HUD’s second mortgage for the discount amount.

You do not need to remember every step on your own. A loan professional and HUD-registered real estate broker can guide you through the parts they handle and tell you what comes next.

Financing, Closing Costs, and Repairs

You can use an FHA loan, VA loan, conventional mortgage, or cash to buy a GNND home. The $100-down benefit is connected to qualifying FHA financing. Some state or local down payment assistance programs may also work with GNND, but every program and lender must approve the combination.

A small down payment does not always mean a small monthly payment. Ask for an estimate that includes the interest rate, mortgage insurance, property taxes, homeowners insurance, homeowners association fees, and possible repair costs. Looking at the full monthly cost can prevent surprises later.

If a temporary rate buydown is available, ask what the payment will be after the temporary period ends. Focus on the permanent loan terms and make sure the long-term payment feels comfortable for your budget.

What If the HUD Home Needs Work?

Some HUD-owned homes need repairs. An FHA 203(k) renovation loan may let you include approved repair costs in your mortgage. Whether this works depends on the home’s condition, the type of repairs, the appraisal, contractor information, and loan rules.

Always consider an independent home inspection. The 50% discount may be valuable, but you still need to understand the roof, heating and cooling systems, plumbing, electrical system, safety concerns, insurance, and possible repair budget.

The 36-Month Primary Residence Requirement

You must use the GNND home as your main home, also called your primary or sole residence, for 36 months. Depending on the home’s condition, HUD may allow you to move in 30, 90, or 180 days after closing. HUD will send a form each year asking you to confirm that you still live there.

This program may not be the right fit if you expect to move soon, rent out the property, or buy it as an investment. The discount is meant for community professionals who plan to live in the neighborhood for at least three years.

Good Neighbor Next Door Program Pros and Cons

The main benefits are the 50% discount, the possible $100-down FHA option, and early access to an eligible HUD home. For the right buyer and property, those benefits can make homeownership much more reachable.

The challenges are the limited number of homes, the short seven-day listing period, the lottery when several buyers are interested, as-is property condition, job and location rules, the second mortgage, and the three-year living requirement.

There is no need to decide based on the benefits alone. Start by checking your eligibility, likely monthly payment, repair risk, and how long you plan to live in the home.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Good Neighbor Next Door only for first-time homebuyers?

No. You do not need to be a first-time buyer. You and your spouse generally cannot own another home when you make the offer or during the previous 12 months.

Can I choose any Colorado home and get 50% off?

No. The discount works only with eligible HUD-owned homes listed through the GNND program in HUD-approved revitalization areas.

Is the down payment always $100?

No. The $100 down payment requires an eligible home and qualifying FHA-insured financing. Other homes and loan types have different down payment rules.

Do I make payments on the silent second mortgage?

No monthly payment or interest is required while you follow the program rules. HUD can release the second mortgage after you complete the three-year living requirement and required forms.

How often do Colorado properties become available?

There is no set schedule. HUD says the number of homes is limited and the available list changes weekly. Getting prepared first can help you act when a suitable home appears.

Explore Current Colorado HUD Home Options

Good Neighbor Next Door can be a powerful opportunity, but you do not have to sort through every rule by yourself. The first step is simply finding out whether your job, location, financing, and current HUD homes might fit together.

The separate FHA $100 Down Sales Incentive may also help some buyers who do not qualify for the GNND 50% discount. Because the option depends on the home and loan, it is important to check the current details before making plans.
